questions.question: List out the schools of Psychology.
questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Define learning and its types.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition: Classical conditioning is a learning process where a neutral stimulus
  • becomes associated with a meaningful stimulus and acquires the capacity to elicit a
  • similar response.
  • Example: A student feels anxious when they hear the school bell because it
  • precedes a difficult exam. The bell (neutral stimulus) becomes associated with the
  • stress of the exam (unconditioned stimulus), eventually causing anxiety (conditioned
  • response).
  • Esteem – self-respect, recognition
questions.final_answer: Esteem – self-respect, recognition

questions.question: Define adolescence in terms of psychological development.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition: Adolescence is a developmental stage between childhood and adulthood
  • characterized by significant physical, cognitive, emotional, and social changes.
  • Psychological Aspects
  • Development of identity and self-concept (Erikson’s “identity vs. role
  • confusion” stage)
  • Increased independence and decision-making ability
  • Emotional instability and mood swings due to hormonal changes
  • Formation of peer relationships and social identity
questions.final_answer: Definition: Adolescence is a developmental stage between childhood and adulthood

questions.question: Analyze the importance of Piaget’s cognitive stages in understanding the behaviour of a child.
questions.solution_html:
• Jean Piaget proposed that children develop through four cognitive stages.
  •  Helps understand how children think differently from adults, not just less intelligently.
  •  Sensor motor stage (0–2 yrs) explains learning through senses and object permanence.
  •  Preoperational stage (2–7 yrs) highlights egocentrism and symbolic thinking.
  •  Concrete operational stage (7–11 yrs) shows logical thinking about concrete objects.
  •  Formal operational stage (11+ yrs) explains abstract and hypothetical thinking.
  •  Assists teachers and social workers in designing age-appropriate interventions.
  •  Helps explain behavioral limitations, such as inability to understand others’ perspectives.
  •  Useful in identifying developmental delays or cognitive impairments.
  •  Supports effective communication by aligning with the child’s level of understanding.
questions.final_answer: Analyze the importance of Piaget’s cognitive stages in understanding the behavior of a child.

questions.question: Explain the application of conformity, compliance, and obedience in understanding the behaviour of an individual.
questions.solution_html:
• Conformity: Changing one’s behavior or beliefs to match group norms.
  • o Example: Dressing a certain way because your peers do.
  • o Shows how group influence shapes attitudes and actions.
  • Compliance: Responding favorably to a direct request.
  • o Example: Donating to a cause when asked, even if you didn’t plan to.
  • o Important in marketing, sales, and social interactions.
  • Obedience: Following orders from an authority figure.
  • o Example: Milgram’s experiment showed how people obey authority
  • even when it conflicts with personal conscience.
  • o Explains behavior in hierarchical settings (e.g., military, workplace).
  • These concepts help in understanding social influence, group dynamics, and the
  • mechanisms behind behavior modification in various contexts.
questions.final_answer: the behaviour of an individual.
